#3273. Own 2 Android phones? Google may let you switch service fast – like iPhone Handoff

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Tech > Services & Software > Operating Systems > Mobile OS > Android

If Android Fast Switch works like iPhone Handoff, one eSIM can be quickly switched between two phones.

In iOS 27, Apple announced iPhone Handoff, a networking feature that allows users to switch cell service between two eSIM-enabled iPhones. Text strings in Google’s SIM Manager app suggest the company is preparing a similar feature for compatible Android phones, according to Android Authority.

Code strings include “Use a SIM on two phones,” and note that the feature will be called Fast Switch. Little information is currently available about the feature’s limitations, including which phones or mobile carriers may not be compatible.

Also: Why your USB-C cables look alike, but work differently – and how to tell them apart

On Apple’s side, any iPhone in the US running iOS 27 with a T-Mobile or Verizon-provided eSIM can use iPhone Handoff. AT&T does not currently support iPhone Handoff.

However, the code strings uncovered by Android Authority show that Android’s Fast Switch will work similarly to iPhone Handoff, in that users must be signed in to both devices under the same Google account for the feature to work.

Strings in Google’s SIM Manager app also point to no sharing between two users, so this feature isn’t a way to circumvent carrier fees by adding service to someone else’s phone for the price of one.

If Fast Switch works anything like iPhone Handoff, which it appears it will, one eSIM can be switched between two phones. So, calls, messages, location services, and other information synced to your Apple ID can remain consistent between two devices.

Also: 5 hidden iOS 27 features that make older iPhones better

Some third-party apps, like banking, communications, or social media, may also remain consistent across the two phones, depending on the app’s syncing behavior.

Features like Apple’s iPhone Handoff and Google’s Fast Switch are ideal for people who regularly use two phones. Business owners and digital creators may want one phone strictly for business purposes and the other for personal use.

Also: Google Wallet turns your Android phone into a digital house key

In that case, one person can keep up with two phones without paying for two phone service lines through their carrier. Still, users will incur a fee, as T-Mobile charges $5/month for iPhone Handoff, while Verizon charges $10/month.

#3272. AirPods 5 vs AirPods Pro 3: Which should you buy this holiday season?

The holiday shopping season is here, and Apple’s AirPods are sure to be one of the most popular gifts. If you’re shopping for AirPods, Apple sells three different models: AirPods 5, AirPods Pro 3, and AirPods Max 2. Here’s how they compare.

9to5Mac is supported by Sony: Score Sony’s ULT Field 1 Bluetooth speaker for 51% off. Powerful bass, room-filling sound, up to 12 hours of battery life, IP67 durability, stereo pairing support, and much more.

AirPods 5 were introduced in September and come in two different versions. Unlike their predecessors, both versions of AirPods 5 offer Active Noise Cancellation. They differ in the charging case, battery life, and volume control. The base model AirPods 5 ($129) come with a case that can only charge via USB-C.

The case for the higher-end AirPods 5 ($149) supports wireless charging and Find My. You also get one extra hour of battery life. The higher-end model also adds on-stem volume control, so you can adjust the volume just by swiping up or down on one of the earbud stems.

Here’s a full comparison between both AirPods 5 models:

The key thing about AirPods 5 is their open-ear design, unlike the in-ear design of the AirPods Pro 3 (more on those later). Even with that open-ear design, AirPods 5 offer incredible Active Noise Cancellation capabilities.

If you are shopping for AirPods 5, I do recommend spending the extra $20 to get the higher-end model. The better charging case alone is worth the extra money. With Find My integration and a built-in speaker, you can track your AirPods and play a sound from the case if you lose them.

If the person you’re shopping for doesn’t like in-ear earbuds, AirPods 5 are an excellent choice.

For most people, though, AirPods Pro 3 are probably the better choice …

AirPods Pro 3 are Apple’s most capable earbuds, even with the introduction of AirPods 5 this year. They offer an in-ear fit and come with five foam-infused silicone ear tip sizes. With that in-ear design, AirPods Pro 3 can offer up to 3x stronger noise cancellation than AirPods 5. In my testing, this difference is notable.

AirPods Pro 3 also offer several other features you won’t find on AirPods 5, including a heart rate sensor for workouts, plus Hearing Test, Hearing Aid, and Hearing Protection features.

I still think AirPods Pro 3 are one of the best products in Apple’s lineup today. I wear mine for multiple hours every single day and can’t imagine life without them. I love the in-ear fit, and the ANC still impresses me, whether I’m at home or somewhere like a coffee shop.

If you know the person you’re shopping for (whether it’s yourself or someone else) likes the in-ear earbud design, I think AirPods Pro 3 are the best option. This is especially true when AirPods Pro 3 are on sale, like they are right now at $179. The price difference between AirPods 5 and AirPods Pro 3 is very small, and you’re getting a much better product.

Finally, we have AirPods Max. These are Apple’s only option for people who want AirPods in an over-ear headphone form factor. Last year, they were pretty hard to recommend since they’d gone five years without a real upgrade.

This year, however, Apple officially introduced AirPods Max 2, bringing modern features to Apple’s high-end headphones. This includes features like Adaptive Audio, Conversation Awareness, Personalized Volume, and more.

AirPods Max 2 are a far more compelling option than AirPods Max were at this time last year. They’re still pricey, but I love the aesthetics and find them very comfortable. There’s something about the premium aluminum design with an elegant Digital Crown that really stands out.

If you’re looking to splurge this holiday season, AirPods Max 2 are a great choice. For more realistic budgets, I think AirPods Pro 3 are the best option.

Are you planning to buy anyone AirPods this holiday season? Are they on your wishlist? Let us know down in the comments.

#3271. Apple reveals daily limits on your Siri AI use – here’s how much you’ll have to pay

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

The more you pay for an iCloud+ plan, the more you’ll be able to use Siri AI and Apple Intelligence for advanced server-side tasks.

Have you been using the new Siri AI? If so, how much? I’ve been turning to it a lot since the release of iOS 27. Well, how we use it — and how often — will soon depend on how much we pay for an iCloud+ plan.

Also: 5 apps I need Siri AI to work with now that it’s open to third-party developers

Apple hasn’t been shy about stating that the use of Siri AI and Apple Intelligence for specific tasks would face daily access limits. Increased limits would be granted based on your iCloud+ subscription. Now the company has revealed how much it will cost you and when the limits will begin.

“Starting with the 2027 software releases, Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features are available for free for users with a supported device set to a supported language,” Apple said on a support page updated November 16. “Some features rely on powerful server models and have limits where increased access is available with eligible iCloud+ plans, starting with the 27.3 release.”

iOS 27.3 is expected to launch in early December, so that’s when the daily usage limits will kick in.

At that point, people with no paid iCloud+ plan and even those with the $0.99-per-month 50 GB plan will be the most limited, with Apple saying only that they’ll face a “Standard Device Limit.”

What is a standard limit? That depends not just on how many times you tap into Siri per day but on what tasks you assign it. Basic Siri commands, such as setting timers and alarms or sending standard text messages, will remain free and unlimited.

Also: Ready for a Siri AI agent? Apple under pressure to upgrade its assistant faster

Advanced Siri and Apple Intelligence tasks will bump into the usage limits. These include the following, according to Apple:

One positive here is that the limits are per device not per account. That means you can use Siri AI and Apple Intelligence with the same account across your iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, Apple TV, and Vision Pro without fear of chewing up too much of your quota.

This all sounds like a way for Apple to steer people to more expensive iCloud+ accounts. But the limits are in place for a key reason. Basic commands are processed on your device, so they don’t require the use of Apple servers. More advanced tasks are processed using server-side AI models, which can feel the strain if too many people access them all at once.

Also: What you’ll pay for AI agents will be wildly variable and unpredictable

How will you know if you use up your daily allotment and what happens then? You’ll receive a notification if you hit your limit for a particular feature category. At that point, you can still give Siri basic tasks to perform. But advanced ones will be paused until your limit resets the next day. Otherwise, Apple is undoubtedly hoping that people who continually run into limits will upgrade to a pricier iCloud+ plan.

By Daniel Sparks – Nov 20, 2026 at 4:23PM EST

10 stocks we like better than Marvell Technology ›

Marvell Technology (MRVL -11.69%) will release results for its fiscal third quarter of 2027 (the period ended Oct. 31, 2026) on Tuesday, Dec. 1, with a conference call at 1:30 p.m. Pacific time.

The chipmaker's stock comes into the report at around $138 as I write, off about 56% from its June 4 record close of $316.43. And most of that drop is recent. Marvell shares ended Oct. 28 at around $252, the last trading day before speculation started about a deal for optical parts maker Lumentum Holdings.

On Nov. 2, the two companies announced an all-stock deal. After it closes, Marvell's current shareholders will own around two-thirds of the combined company. The growth stock is down about 45% from that Oct. 28 close.

The Dec. 1 report will be Marvell's first full quarterly update since it agreed to buy Lumentum. And if the past three years are any guide, the shares might make a big move the day after.

Marvell reports after the market closes, so the reaction shows up in the next day's trading. Here are its last 12 reports, the stock's close-to-close move the next day, and the revenue growth management guided for the following quarter over the quarter just reported.

Data source: Yahoo Finance and Marvell. Calculations by author.

Shares dropped the next day seven times and climbed five times.

And the moves were big either way. The average swing was around 12%, and seven of the 12 moves topped 10%.

Interestingly, the quarters themselves were almost never to blame. In all 12 reports, Marvell's revenue came in above the midpoint of its guidance.

I think the outlook mattered more. In the six reports in which management guided to next-quarter revenue growth of 6% or lower (with one guide for a decline), the stock fell the next day five times, with an average drop of around 9%.

In the six where it guided for about 8% or more, shares climbed four times, with an average gain of about 6%.

But six reports on either side doesn't prove much, and the pattern has a clear exception. In August 2026, management guided to third-quarter revenue of $3.15 billion, up 15% from the second quarter's $2.74 billion, the second-largest increase in the table. The stock still dropped 10% the next day.

A possible reason is that expectations had risen with the tech company's share price, which had more than tripled since the March 2026 report.

This time, the quarter itself could hold even less surprise than normal. When it announced the Lumentum deal on Nov. 2, Marvell said preliminary third-quarter revenue was in line with its guidance. It kept the $3.15 billion midpoint and tightened the range to plus or minus 2%.

That puts the focus on the fiscal fourth quarter, and the bar is high for a chipmaker helped by demand for artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure. Marvell's revenue climbed 22% year over year in the final quarter of fiscal 2026. Growth then rose to 28% and 37% in the first two quarters of fiscal 2027. And the $3.15 billion third-quarter midpoint means growth of around 52%, an acceleration for a third straight quarter.

"[W]e expect our revenue growth to accelerate further through the remainder of fiscal 2027," Marvell CEO Matt Murphy said in the company's fiscal second-quarter earnings release.

For growth to keep accelerating in the fiscal fourth quarter, revenue would have to exceed $3.4 billion, or about 7% above the third-quarter midpoint. In other words, a guide that just keeps pace with the third quarter might land right around the line that has split the stock's past reactions.

In the end, I'd expect a big move on Dec. 2 either way, and a down day has been a bit more common than an up day. But I wouldn't read much into one day's move when the Lumentum deal isn't expected to close until the first half of 2028.

Personally, I'd pay more attention to the size of the fourth-quarter guide than to the stock's reaction to it. Shares trade at around 20 times the earnings analysts expect for fiscal 2028, a price that seems reasonable if growth continues to accelerate. And if shares drop again on a guide that still shows accelerating growth, I think the lower price might be worth considering for investors who can ride out more swings like these.

#3267. Ray Dalio says Bessent move is sign that a debt crisis is getting closer; recommends gold and bitcoin

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's debt buyback announcement this week fits into a broader pattern that can signal a forthcoming crisis, according to billionaire investor Ray Dalio.

The Bridgewater Associates founder said Bessent's plan to increase government debt purchases may portend trouble for the U.S. economy. Coupled with the Japanese government reducing its U.S. bond market exposure and surging long-dated American bond yields, Dalio said investors may want to prepare their portfolios for increased risk by owning cryptocurrencies and gold.

"I am confident that the government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote in a LinkedIn post published Friday. "If this is not dealt with now, the debts will build up to levels where they can't be managed without great trauma."

Dalio noted that the Treasury Department has "only limited capacity" to buy back bonds. Bessent told CNBC on Thursday that his team was going to "make a market" and that the purchases would likely top $4 billion.

The U.S. is spending about 40% more than it's bringing in, resulting in the burgeoning budget deficit, Dalio said. The U.S. budget deficit topped $432 billion in July, but Bessent told CNBC that it's likely peaked under President Donald Trump's administration.

Bessent said in the interview that a team was looking at ways to shrink spending by hundreds of billions of dollars. But Dalio said there is "very little ability" to do so given that it is either committed or considered essential.

After years of overspending, Dalio said total debt now dwarfs what the U.S. brings in each year. If the U.S. government was a business, Dalio said debt service payments would come in at roughly $11 trillion — about 200% of annual revenue.

Dalio, 77, warned the cost of repaying principal and servicing the debt will only grow over time.

To solve this, Dalio said the U.S. needs to carefully employ a three-part strategy to get the budget deficit down to 3% of gross domestic product.

First, Dalio said the U.S. government needs to reduce its spending. Second, he said tax revenue needs to be raised. Finally, the New York native and Harvard Business School alumni said lower interest rates were needed.

"All three need to happen concurrently so as to prevent any one from being too large," Dalio said. "If any one is too large, the adjustment will be traumatic."

Dalio cautioned against ramming through these adjustments by "force." For instance, "it would be very bad if the Federal Reserve unnaturally forced interest rates down," he said.

Dalio said it's important to to take steps now, while the economy is healthy. An economy in recession requires increased government spending, he said.

Dalio said the exact timing of a debt crisis can be swayed by variables ranging from military conflict to political change. On its current trajectory, the U.S. could enter such a crisis in as early as one year or as late as five. "My guess, which I suppose will be a bad one, is that it will come in three years, give or take two, if the course we're on is not changed."

To prepare, Dalio recommended investors are underweight debt assets, such as bonds.

As much as 10% to 15% of a portfolio could land in gold, as well as "a bit" of bitcoin, the hedge fund founder said.

Dalio's post came at the tail end of a volatile week for U.S. financial markets. Rising long-term Treasury yields have pressured stocks, leading the S&P 500 to snap a a three-week-long advance.

#3266. I asked Gemini Notebook to ‘make me a site’ from my notes – it was satisfying

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

A new Gemini Notebook feature lets you create interactive sites from intricate data.

Google’s Gemini can now turn your notes and other sources in your Gemini Notebook (previously called NotebookLM) into interactive pages or sites to help you better process complicated information.

Complete with flashcards, dashboards, and colorful panels, the sites make it easier to study and understand intricate concepts. I tested the feature, announced Tuesday, to see how efficient it is at creating a navigable site that is actually helpful and stays loyal to sources.

Also: 4 ways Anthropic’s new Claude Sheets beat using a Google Sheets connector in my tests

Because Notebooks are built with the sources you provide, like textbooks, files, or notes, the sites are created with the data that is in your Gemini Notebook. Notebook has three tabs: Sources, Chat, and Studio. The site option is in the Studio tab, listed under what you can create.

If you’re taking a college class, you could put all the information you need to prepare for a test and use the interactive site as a study guide that you can share with others.

To test this, I gave Notebook the following prompt:

“Make me a site that visually explains how cellular respiration works, breaking down each stage with interactive diagrams and self-check flashcards.”

Since I’m not in a class that would give me those study materials, I gave Gemini online sources to use for this. Gemini cited the sources in my notebook, then spent a few minutes creating the interactive site. Gemini will give you a quick update when it’s done, including a summary of the source information as it pertains to your request and instructions on where to find the site.

Also: I checked Gemini’s new Memory summary to see what it knew about me – how to see and edit yours

As promised, my cellular respiration notes were complete and organized on an interactive, visually appealing site that was easy to navigate. The coolest feature on the site was the flashcards, which you can hover over to see which ones you’ve studied.

The interactive site feature is now available to Gemini Notebook users and will soon come to the mobile app. As someone who knows very little about coding, I was pretty satisfied to see the information Gemini put together presented in explorable, easy-to-understand tabs on a site.

#3265. Apple Watch Series 12: Four standout features make me glad I upgraded

I upgraded to an Apple Watch Series 12 this fall (now $329 on Amazon), and there are four main features that make me especially glad I did.

The Apple Watch was overdue for a chip update, with Apple skipping any changes last year and not having any true performance upgrades since the S9.

I’m happy to report that the new S11 chip appears much faster and more capable than its predecessor, the S10.

Everyday tasks on Apple Watch Series 12 just feel fast. And Siri AI, a tentpole addition in watchOS 27, very much feels made for this latest hardware. Siri was sluggish on older hardware in my testing, but it performs much more like I’d hoped on Series 12.

The new Health Sensing System makes Apple Watch Series 12 better at tracking key metrics like heart rate and steps. But this isn’t a case where accuracy is the only improvement.

Because of the new health sensors, Series 12 offers three complications not available before:

The complications let you see up-to-date readings on your current heart rate, step count, and readiness score right from your watch face. These are very welcome additions that meaningfully improve the Apple Watch’s health and wellness feature set.

I’ve been using the watchOS 27.3 beta, which adds a new Siri Recap feature for Series 12 models that I really love.

Siri Recap ambiently takes notes on your conversations throughout your day and creates high-level Apple Intelligence–generated summaries that you can use later to jog your memory, so you can stay present in the moment.

Most of what Siri documents, I’ll never need to reference and it gets deleted automatically. But for those times I have trouble remembering a key piece of information, I’ve found Siri Recap a very convenient addition.

Apple Watch Series 12 offers largely the same battery life as Series 11, though it will last 25% longer for outdoor workouts.

More battery is always nice, but I’m especially a fan of the faster charging available on Series 12. Here’s how it stacks up to Series 11:

I wear my Apple Watch to bed and generally try to top it off quickly in the evening, but I’m not always great at giving it much time on the charger. With faster charging support on Series 12, my poor planning isn’t a problem.

Apple Watch Series 12 is now only $329 on Amazon, down from $399.

Have you upgraded to Apple Watch Series 12? Why or why not? Let us know in the comments.

Subsequent price hikes make it a tougher call

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Flagship phones are the prized devices that pair bleeding-edge hardware with unmatched performance across the board. While the iPhone 18 Pro Max, Galaxy S26 Ultra, and Pixel 11 Pro XL lead the way as some of the best phones you can buy, you don't always need to spend $1,299 or more to get a top-tier experience. That’s why I'm turning my attention to their slightly more accessible siblings.

I've spent months testing the iPhone 17, Galaxy S26, and Pixel 11, putting them through different matchups and photo face-offs — all to see how they perform against one another. Normally, these base flagships represent the sweet spot for shoppers looking to save money without sacrificing core performance, flagship cameras, or robust software suites. But given the recent price hikes across the board, their value propositions have shifted.

If your budget is dead set at under $1,000, choosing the right daily driver comes down to more than just looking at a spec sheet or briefly checking them out tethered at a carrier store. I’m breaking down where each model shines, where they fall short, and which $899 phone is truly worth buying.

6.3-inch Super Retina XDR (2,622 x 1,206)

48MP main (f/1.78), 48MP ultrawide (f/2.2)

50MP (f/1.8) main, 12MP (f/2.2) ultrawide, 10MP (f/2.4) telephoto w/3x optical zoom

48MP (f/1.7) main, 13MP (f/2.2) ultrawide, 10.8MP (f/3.1) telephoto w/5x optical zoom

Cobalt Violet, Sky Blue, Black, White (online exclusive: Silver Shadow, Pink Gold)

Despite being the oldest contender in this lineup, launching back in the fall of 2025, the iPhone 17 remains one of the best values in Apple's catalog. It is still available due to how the company shifted its release schedule this past September to launch the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Duo first — with the iPhone 18 rumored to launch early next year alongside the iPhone 18e.

When it launched, it came with an attractive $799 starting cost that I specifically noted offered one of the best bang-for-the-buck values around. But it’s since been given a $100 price hike that now puts it at $899, which is shocking considering how phones tend to get price drops a year after they’re launched — and not the other way around.

Still, the iPhone 17 represents the biggest leap forward for an entry-level iPhone in years over the previous iPhone 16. Apple finally ditched the sluggish 60Hz panel in favor of a buttery-smooth 120Hz ProMotion display, all while doubling the base storage to 256GB.

Apple’s A19 chip is a generation behind the latest silicon, but it hasn't missed a beat in my testing. Apps continue to launch instantaneously, and UI animations are just as fluid as ever with iOS 27, plus it handles demanding games without breaking a sweat.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Obviously, the new software brings more Apple Intelligence features and the new Siri AI. As much as I appreciate them, however, Siri still doesn’t have the same level of functionality that I get from Gemini. For example, most of its cross-app functions are limited to native apps — and not third-party ones.

When it comes to taking photos and video, its 48MP main camera continues to lead the way — consistently delivering crisp shots and holding its own remarkably well under low-light conditions. It’s paired with a 48MP ultrawide, but all zoom is handled by the main camera through sensor and digital cropping. As a result, it lacks the power to resolve fine details compared to its rivals.

Overall, I still like the iPhone 17, and it still saves you money over the $1,099 iPhone 18 Pro. Given the price hike for a year-old model, though, it’s hard to recommend at this point unless you intend on staying in the Apple ecosystem.

Just like Apple, Samsung upped the price of its base Galaxy S26 flagship model — going from $899 when it launched this past January to a whopping $999 now. This is a tougher pill to swallow because the previous Galaxy S25 was $799, meaning there was already a $100 price hike for the S26, and it’s technically $200 more than its predecessor.

Still, it’s worth mentioning that Samsung at least doubled the base storage to 256GB. And if that’s not enough, it gets the same chip as its pricier Galaxy S26 Ultra sibling: the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy. That translates to heavyweight gaming performance and effortless multitasking on its 6.3-inch 120Hz AMOLED display, which hits a blinding 1,950 nits in our testing and remains visible under the midday sun.

What makes the package more satisfying are Samsung's ambitious new Agentic AI features and One UI 8.5 upgrades, including genuinely helpful additions like the new Photo Assist tools, which let me describe what photo edits I want to make on an image, and Now Nudge, which makes the phone feel more proactive in daily use. With Google Gemini on board, I’ve even used the AI to place a Dunkin’ Donuts order via DoorDash — all through a simple voice command.

I also love how the Galaxy S26 is the productivity workhorse of the trio, offering intuitive side-by-side app multitasking on the phone and greater flexibility with Samsung DeX. The latter’s really helpful because I can get a PC-like experience when I connect it to an external monitor, which isn’t something I can do with the iPhone 17.

On the camera front, Samsung mostly stuck with the same triple-camera hardware as before — a 50MP main sensor, 12MP ultrawide, and 10MP telephoto with 3x optical zoom. While still photos don't represent a massive leap over last year, having a dedicated telephoto lens gives it a clear zoom advantage over the iPhone 17. For video shooters, I love the new Horizon Lock video stabilization and how it keeps handheld footage dead level no matter how much I jostle or tilt the phone while shooting.

There are still areas for improvement with the Galaxy S26, like its shorter battery life and a boring design that has been recycled countless times with minimal changes. However, the thing that stings the most is its $999 price tag. Sure, it’s one of the most well-rounded devices here, combining compelling hardware with a superb software suite, but it’s harder to love when it's the most expensive phone in this matchup.

First and foremost, the Google Pixel 11 is technically the latest release out of the bunch and remains highly competitive with an $899 starting cost — up from the Pixel 10’s $799 price. At least Google softens the blow by doubling the starting storage to 256GB.

Beyond that, however, the core hardware barely changes from last year. It retains a solid, durable design with a 40% thinner camera bar that sits virtually flush in a case, and its 6.3-inch Actua OLED display is remarkably bright — hitting 2,480 nits in our testing. Plus, with built-in PixelSnap charging, it matches the iPhone 17 in offering native magnetic wireless charging without the need for an add-on case.

Where the Pixel 11 stumbles, though, is raw performance. Even though the Tensor G6 is the newest chip in this matchup, it still trails both the A19 and Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 in benchmarks and graphics processing. Google tries to make up for it with software, rolling out genuinely useful Gemini AI features like Rambler voice dictation, Proactive Assistance, and a revamped Pixel Desktop Mode that rivals Samsung DeX when I hook it up to an external monitor.

On the camera side, Google stuck with the same triple-camera hardware as before — a 48MP main sensor, 13MP ultrawide, and a 10.8MP telephoto lens. While everyday shots look nearly identical to the Pixel 10, having a dedicated 5x optical zoom gives it the strongest zoom performance in this trio, effortlessly outreaching the Galaxy S26's 3x lens and the iPhone 17's digital crop.

New camera tools that I appreciate include Magic Capture, which leans on AI to pick out picture-perfect shots for me so I can remain immersed in the moment. Another helpful tool, Creator Suite, makes it even easier to vlog and record selfie videos thanks to a built-in teleprompter. The Pixel 11 isn’t perfect, but its $899 price tag makes it hard to resist.

All three phones feature crisp 6.3-inch displays with up to a 120Hz refresh rate, making them equally smooth for scrolling and gaming. However, our lab testing reveals a huge gap in peak brightness. The Pixel 11 easily takes the crown at 2,480 nits, noticeably outshining the Galaxy S26 at 1,950 nits and leaving the iPhone 17 trailing at 1,505 nits.

Under direct sunlight, the Pixel 11 is far easier to read without forcing me to shade it with my hand, whereas the iPhone 17 can look significantly dimmer by comparison.

3DMark Wild Life Original Unlimited (score/fps)

Personally, I think all three phones feel snappy enough for everyday tasks such as browsing, streaming, and jumping between apps. Our benchmark testing, however, shows a clear powerhouse amongst the trio.

The Galaxy S26’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 takes the overall performance crown, leading the pack in Geekbench 6 multi-core testing with a score of 10,778 and dominating graphics with 28,548 (171.6 fps) in 3DMark Wild Life Original Unlimited. The iPhone 17’s older A19 chip holds its own remarkably well, while the Pixel 11’s Tensor G6 regrettably falls behind despite being the newest silicon in this trio.

This doesn't mean the Pixel 11 feels sluggish in casual tasks, but if you play graphics-intensive games or push your phone with heavy video editing, the Galaxy S26 and iPhone 17 give you better sustained performance.

When it comes to battery endurance, the iPhone 17 and Pixel 11 are virtually neck and neck, while the Galaxy S26 trails behind. In our battery benchmark test, the iPhone 17 edges out the win at 12 hours and 47 minutes, closely followed by the Pixel 11 at 12 hours and 45 minutes. Meanwhile, the Galaxy S26 lags more than an hour behind at 11 hours and 28 minutes.

The iPhone 17 widens its lead when it’s time to plug in as well. In fact, it reaches 39% in 15 minutes and 71% after 30 minutes of wired charging. By comparison, the Galaxy S26 hits 29% at the 15-minute mark and 57% in 30 minutes, while the Pixel 11 gets to 27% and 52%, respectively.

After putting them through their paces, I would actually recommend buying the Google Pixel 11. Price hikes across the board make these phones a tougher value proposition than they used to be, but the Pixel 11 delivers the most well-rounded experience for the money.

It’s not the fastest phone on paper, nor does it charge the quickest. However, it easily outshines the competition with the brightest display in direct sunlight, solid real-world all-day battery life, and the most versatile camera system, thanks to its dedicated 5x optical zoom and genuinely useful Creator Suite tools.

Throw in built-in PixelSnap magnetic charging, Pixel Desktop Mode, and the smartest Gemini AI features at my disposal, and the Pixel 11 gives you the best bang for your buck without forcing you to spend over $1,000.

#3263. Google is making it easier to opt out of Gemini AI model training – here’s how

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

You’ll soon be able to turn off Gemini model training but still retain access to your previous chats with Google’s AI.

Also: I checked Gemini’s new Memory summary to see what it knew about me

In a change set to roll out in the coming weeks, you’ll be able to put the brakes on Gemini model training without losing access to your previous conversations with the AI. Here’s how this works now — and how it will work down the road.

Currently, Gemini offers a setting called Keep Activity that controls not only whether and for how long your chats are saved but also whether they’re used to train the AI. You can’t separate the two.

To correct this problem, Google will replace Keep Activity with two new settings. With the first setting, you’ll be able to keep or delete your past chats and choose how long your history will be saved. With the second setting, you’ll be able to decide whether your chats, including all text and attachments, will be used for model training.

Also: I asked Gemini Notebook to ‘make me a site’ from my notes

“With this change, you will be able to keep your history while independently controlling generative AI model training,” Google said in an announcement shared to Gemini users via email.

Here’s how this will play out. If your Keep Activity setting is off when this change is made, both new settings will be off. If your Keep Activity setting is on, both new settings will be on. That means you’ll need to head to Gemini’s Settings if you wish to opt out of model training but still be able to view and access your previous chats.

ChatGPT offers a setting called “Improve the model for everyone,” which is double-speak for model training. But this is easy enough to turn off. Microsoft Copilot provides settings for “Training on conversation activity” and “Training on voice conversations,” both of which you can disable to opt out of model training. Claude’s AI training option is turned off by default. But you can always control this by checking the setting for “Help improve our AI models.”

How do you view the long-term impact of the foundation models on the Robotaxi industry, and where will be sustainable competitive advantages reside as AI capability continue to evolve?

Xuan Li: Xu, you want to take the question?

Xu Han: I think let you take the question, or I take the question. Who wants? Okay, I will take the question.

Xuan Li: Yeah, it is on frontier LLM, I think. It is better.

Xu Han: I understand this, but I take this question. Yeah, I just feel like, yeah, a little bit due to the jet lag, I am a little bit kind of tired, but I think I will answer this question. So first of all, it is a very heated discussion and debate, so it is kind of Thank you for this great question. I think this question is really great. In a broad way, you can say everything can be replaced by AI. Nowadays, whatever, we cannot safely say that anything cannot be replaced by AI.

But if you look into details, okay, so we can see that the general-purpose model are very good at high-level tasks like reasoning and coding, but controlling a car is completely different problem. It is just like, why we believe the humanoid robot can replace all the top-level surgeon to do the surgery for patients, okay? It is still in a sci-fi movie. In a recent public test, even the most advanced general-purpose model could barely complete a single lap of empty parking lot. Driving is a matter of life and death. The system has to respond within milliseconds with absolute precision, and there's no room for mistakes. Let me emphasize, there's no room for mistakes.

Auto-grade chips with high power limit. This kind of thing really requires lots of technology to really work on it. All of the hardware for the autonomous driving vehicle are purposely built. I don't think a general AI model can be run on this kind of platform within next three or four years. These are just some general discussion. People talk about in a general way, but come to the field, and we studied large language model very carefully. By the way, I think I'm in a position to say so because my background is in really AI. I think, for the general-purpose build foundation model, they currently don't have a chance.

Because we have to have a very compact model on it, and the precision is key. Over time, foundation model may gradually improve, but there's a long way to go. I think in the near future, as a five-year framework, I don't see any chance for this general-purpose AI can write a autonomous driving algorithm and replace the current algorithm. Within five years, if you look at our plan, we have already deployed our Robotaxi fleet, covered global market. We will keep an eye on this general-purpose algorithm. As I mentioned, we have built out all the physical AI-relevant infrastructure. If the general-purpose LLM can work, I think we are among the first group of companies who adopt this technology.

Overall, we embrace this technology, and we are confident this company will be the first pioneer who adopt this technology, and we will remain as a leading position. As the first mover company, we will remain at our current position and enjoy the consequential profit and revenue. That's my answers to this question. Thank you. Great question. Very insightful.

Xuan Li: Just to add on a little bit more to this question. A better model doesn't alone, it doesn't put the driverless car on the road. What we do quite intensively is discussing with the regulator. Regulator, they need to approve a validated system in each specific market, and it's not the model who's doing this. The real heavy lifting is to build the trust, integrating the software, hardware, testing across cities, countries, and proving safety over millions of kilometers. Then we have to operate it at scale on everyday basis. That's why we have spent the years to build. Now we have permit in nine countries. We are running in 13 countries, in 60 cities.

That's actually a key moat that we have building over the years. Thank you.

Operator: Thank you. We will now take the next question from the line of Yuqian Ding from HSBC. Please go ahead.

Yuqian Ding: Thank you, team. Yuqian here. It is actually a two-parting question on the China L2++ market. We are seeing the competition is getting tense, OEMs are struggling, probably more pressure on pricing. How would management evaluating the competition landscape going forward? Could you also share your order growth as in both volume and pricing term? Thank you.

Xu Han: I think I will take this question. First of all, I have to admit, the competition is intensive. Automakers are very cost conscious, and the industry really want to bring smart driving to more buyers. We see a big opportunity, because currently the urban navigation or autopilot penetration is still low, and we see a big market, big opportunity. There is plenty of room and long-term growth. I think our goal is to make smart driving, including urban navigation, available to everyone, both in China and for the overseas market. We can do that because our cost is significantly lower than our peers. Our one-stage end-to-end solution actually just shares the technology we developed with our L4 driverless operation.

You can see the track record. We won eight titles in China's intelligent driving competition, which basically means our ADAS system is superior. It is much better than our competitors. We have got more than 20 mass production deployments, and we have more volumes to come. We are really confident, actually, in future for the growth. Overall, I think L2++ plays a very clear role in our strategy, and it builds our brand with our consumers and grows our driving data. We basically use our L2++ application and our L4 Robotaxi operation leverage onto each other, sharing the data and help each other to improve the algorithms.

In the future, the goal of development of L2++ is it requires a higher and higher computational platform, which can adopt more and more advanced L4 level technology, which WeRide have developed over the past 10 years and is one of the best company in L4. Overall, I think WeRide will remain its leading position in ADAS, and more and more OEMs will adopt our system. I look forward to take even larger market share in ADAS market. As I mentioned before, the penetration for NOA will keep on growing, I think, to 100%, because most of the people, they do not want to drive by themselves. They just want to rely on the system help to drive.

Overall, with our technology, we are confident that we will remain at our current leading position. Thank you for this question.

Operator: Thank you. We will now take the next question from the line of Yuan Tao from CSC. Please go ahead.

Yuan Tao: Hi. Good evening. I have a question about the UE. WeRide achieved positive unit economics in Guangzhou this quarter. Can you walk us through how you define UE and what costs are included, and roughly how they break down? Thank you.

Xuan Li: I will take this question. Okay. Reaching unit economic breakeven is actually a really important milestone for us. I will be very precise about what it includes. On the revenue side, we count the net ride-hailing revenue after the refunds. On the cost side, we include all the major cost items. That includes vehicle depreciation, including battery, all the way to autonomous driving hardwares, and also the charging, the salary for remote, and also the ground supporting staff. Also, there is cleaning, maintenance, insurance, parking, network, and telecom fees. Everything is included. Slightly less than half of the total cost goes to the vehicle depreciation related, and the rest is other items.

That is a very comprehensive measure of all the cost items. In Guangzhou, we achieved the positive UE for the first time, with an average order of 21 daily order per vehicle. There are three things that are actually driving this. First of all, it is the high utilization, longer average trip distance, and also a higher efficient staff-to-vehicle ratio for both remote assistance and ground support. We will keep improving those ratios so that the per-vehicle labor costs stay as low as possible. Also, when the fleet is growing, we just want to make sure that the per-vehicle labor cost can be really low.

Like I say, we can already achieve a positive UE in Guangzhou, and for overseas, the structure will be even more attractive. Under our asset-light business model, the partners own vehicles, and then we do not carry the CapEx for the vehicles. On top of that, we bring what we learned in China to our overseas markets. For now, we have already improved on the remote assistant efficiency in the Middle East to more than one to 10, and we are also optimizing the dispatch system, the maintenance process, and the fleet management playbooks. In short, China is one of the most demanding operating environments in the world.

Applying this experience abroad helps us to, and our partners as well, to streamlining the cost and launch new markets faster. This matters even more in places like Europe, where the initial launch, like say, the labor and energy costs can be very high. So yeah, this is a key milestone for us to reach, unit breakeven in China. Yeah. Thank you.

Operator: Thank you. We will now take the next question from the line of Dongbin Han from Huatai Securities. Please go ahead.

Xuan Li: Actually, I think we are running out of time. Maybe we can just take one more question, one last question.

Dongbin Han: Okay, thank you. Hi, management. Due to time limits, I will keep it brief. Congratulations to this strong quarter. My two questions. First, do you have enough cash to reach breakeven in 2029? Which expenses are temporary and which will be recurring? Second, will the company issue new shares or conduct a placement under the current share price? Thanks so much.

Xuan Li: Okay, I will be brief about this. To answer the first question, yes, we have enough cash to reach breakeven in 2029. Yes, like we just mentioned over the call, we ended the quarter with CNY 4.7 billion in cash reserve. More importantly, in the fourth quarter, the receivable collection and the prepayment should keep our cash reserve roughly stable as the same as now. We expect cash burn to also fall to around CNY 1 billion in 2027, and it will decline even further in 2028. In 2028, that is when we expect we will have the first-ever quarterly positive free cash flow.

With that, if everything goes according to the plan, in 2029, while we can expect positive free cash flow for the full year, we still have more than CNY 1 billion in cash. That is the runway, what we are thinking about this. For the. Just now you also asked about the temporary items. The one-off items will be, like say, for the last quarter, it is the first half performance bonus and upfront payment for our next generation Robotaxi. Those are the one-off. The stage-specific investment, like say, the computing cluster, we will still build some, especially in Europe and in the Middle East, depending on. It is actually really according to the deployment schedule.

Those costs are spread over a much larger revenue base. What the recurring costs will going to be, like say, the R&D stuff and then the ongoing, the model training, those will be the ongoing recurring items. We think we validate unit economic in each market before we really scale in the market, so that will keep us the cash burn under control. In short, we do have full confidence in reaching breakeven in 2029, and the revenue growth really rallies and continues. The last question, I think you also asked about the issue new share.

As we just mentioned, we think the current valuation does not reflect the company's true value, and we will not carry out the issuance or placement at the current valuation. We won't do it. Our priority is really to improve cash flow through the business itself, scaling over using our asset-light L4 business overseas, our growing L2++/L3 production deliveries, and also from Jingshuo data set services. Those will help us to move steadily towards positive cash flow. Thank you.

Operator: Thank you. Due to time constraints, I will conclude the call today. Thank you for your participation in today's conference. This does conclude the program. You may now disconnect.

#3260. Your Googlebook just got a Chrome update – 5 new features

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

The Chrome update includes more useful vertical tabs, easier screen sharing, and some handy keyboard shortcuts.

On Monday, Google rolled out an M157 update for the Chrome web browser on Googlebook OS, with a handful of new features and performance boosts to streamline your workflow and browsing experience.

While the first Googlebooks on the market have received mixed reviews, these features could help the laptops gain more useful features in Chrome that other browsers already offer.

Also: Googlebooks? The best laptop for Android users is something else

Here are the five new Chrome features on Googlebook OS to know about.

If you’ve ever had to share your screen on a video call, you know how irritating it can be to switch tabs without having to repeatedly start and stop sharing. This Chrome update adds a tab-sharing controls bar; when you share a browser tab in a video call, Chrome will display a persistent control bar at the top of the window so you can “Stop sharing” or “Share this tab instead” from any tab.

Also: 6 Chrome default settings I changed to instantly

When you hover over a collapsed vertical tab rail with your mouse or trackpad, it will expand, so you can read full tab titles, switch tabs, or manage groups. The rail will collapse again when you move the cursor away.

This auto-expand feature is enabled by default. If you want to turn it off or on, go to Settings > Appearance > Tab position > “Auto expand tabs on hover,” or right-click the vertical tab rail.

The Chrome update allows you to manually resize your vertical tab bar to view longer page titles when needed. The browser will remember your custom tab width, even after you open a new window or restart the browser. (You’ll just need to turn “Auto expand tabs on hover” off for it to work.)

The system’s “Save As” file picker is now enabled by default for menu save actions, such as “Save link as” and “Save image as,” so you can more easily rename files and select a destination folder. This includes Google Drive or external storage.

Also: Google Chrome running slow? 5 easy ways to speed it up fast

Outside of these new features, a few of Chrome M157’s performance fixes include the ability to press Ctrl+L to reveal and select web addresses; keeping your bookmarks bar visible in fullscreen mode and while screen sharing; better media controls while using Picture-in-Picture mode; and the ability to partially translate PDFs within your browser.

If you have Chrome set up to automatically download and install updates, you won’t have to lift a finger to take advantage of the new features and performance boosts.

But if you’ve disabled automatic updates, you can manually update by selecting the three-dot menu in the top-right corner of your Chrome window and navigating to Help > About Google Chrome > Relaunch.

Also: My week with new Googlebooks: The good, the bad, and the promising

If the Relaunch option is greyed out or nowhere to be found, you’re running on the latest version of Chrome. And if you were working on something before the update, don’t worry: Chrome will save your open tabs and reopen them automatically when you restart.

#3259. iOS 27 lets you use two iPhones with the same phone number

9to5Mac is brought to you by Tello Mobile. Switching to Tello Mobile can bring the cost of your plan down to as little as $5 a month, or an unlimited plan for just $25 a month, all on America’s largest 5G network. See all of the available plans at tello.com.

Among iOS 27’s many new features is a great change for anyone with multiple iPhones: you can now keep the same phone number on two iPhones via iPhone Handoff.

With iOS 27, Apple introduces big AI upgrades like Siri AI, plus exciting new features for apps like Wallet, Messages, Notes, and also CarPlay and AirPods.

But the update also has a lot of smaller, more niche improvements.

One such addition is iPhone Handoff, which enables switching seamlessly between two iPhones using the same phone number.

After iPhone Handoff is set up, one iPhone becomes the main iPhone and the other iPhone becomes the secondary iPhone that shares the number. Your main iPhone should be the one you use most often. Some carrier services, like Call Forwarding and Caller ID, and carrier account management can only be managed on your main iPhone. Contact your carrier for more details.

To move between your main iPhone and secondary iPhone, simply unlock the device that you want to start using — your phone number will automatically become active on that device. The message “Switched to this iPhone” will display at the top of your screen to confirm it’s now active. Your phone number will only be active on one iPhone at a time when using iPhone Handoff.

Most users will never need this feature. But if you’re someone who, for whatever reason, has separate devices that you want on the same number, iOS 27 has the solution.

But the carriers don’t unless you pay them.

If you’re trying to decide between an iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro, perhaps iPhone Handoff is Apple’s subtle way of saying: “Why choose?”

So far carrier support is limited (here’s the latest list), but Apple plans to expand iPhone Handoff to more carriers soon.

Do you have a need to use the same phone number on multiple iPhones? For what reason? Let us know in the comments.

#3257. Goodbye, Gemini Gems: How to use Google’s new Skills – and share them

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Google is retiring Gemini Gems. Here's what to do to access the same tools as Skills.

Google is replacing Gemini Gems with Skills starting Nov. 17, 2026, and it’s carrying over features that let you share Skills and add files from Google products.

Google has announced that it’s turning Gems, a Gemini feature that lets you create customizable AI chatbots, into Skills, which let you create custom instructions for Gemini. Any Gems you have created will automatically convert, but you can transfer them manually if you want to start using them now.

To help with the transition, Google revealed that two Gems features are moving, too: the ability to share creations and to include Drive, Notebook, and Photos files as part of your Skill’s instructions.

While the Gemini Gems feature is technically going away, any Gems you’ve created aren’t.

If you access the Gems portion of Gemini (since the feature is on the way out, you now have to access this through Settings), you’ll see a message that says “Starting November 17, 2026, we’ll automatically begin migrating all of your Gems to Skills.” (The cutoff date for accessing your Gems will be Dec. 16, 2026. Workspace business, enterprise, and non-profit accounts will get cut off in March 2027, and Workspace education accounts will be cut off in June 2027.)

A Gemini Skill functions much the same as a Gem. You describe specific situations when Gemini should use the Skill automatically and tell Gemini what you want the Skill to do (it’s best to give specific examples of output). Google gives the example of a marketing team sharing a brand-voice skill that references their brand guidelines doc in Drive, or a team lead sharing an onboarding skill based on the team handbook.

The biggest difference is that Gems were standalone chats, while Skills are custom instructions that work in any conversation.

You can create as many Skills as you want, but only 100 can be active at a time.

To get users familiar with Skills, Google is bringing over two features from Gems.

First, you can now share any Skill with other users. When you share a Skill, you can choose whether the other person has permission to edit or view only. To share a Skill, go to the three-bar menu in the top left > Customize > Skills. You can view or change permissions from that screen.

Also: I checked Gemini’s new Memory summary to see what it knew about me – how to see and edit yours

When a Skill is added, Gemini can use it automatically, or you can @mention it in chat to trigger it. One small caveat, though: you can only share Skills through the Gemini web app at the moment, not the mobile app.

Additionally, when you’re creating a Gemini Skill, you can choose to include files of up to 100MB from other Google products like Drive, Photos, and Notebook, along with files from your local device. Gemini will reference these files every time the Skill runs and update in real time, Google says. These features existed with Gems; Google is just moving them to Skills to make the new feature more comparable.

If you experience pain at any time, stop and rest. If you're working with an injury or health condition, or you're currently pregnant or postnatal, I recommend seeking advice before starting this exercise.

Both cases share ESR’s Flex Stand, and it’s one of the most innovative and versatile parts of the lineup. It’s a 180-degree rotating stand made from zinc alloy, so it holds its shape even after months of propping up your iPhone. A precision hinge with damping control lets it open smoothly and lock at the angle you choose, whether the iPhone Duo is folded or unfolded, and ESR says it has passed 3,000 open-and-close tests. In real life, that means propping the iPhone Duo open on a desk for a video call or on an airplane tray table for a movie, then using the stand as a grip when you’re holding it.

Both cases add extra hinge protection and raised edges where a foldable is most exposed. If you follow our MagSafe Monday column, you know magnetic strength really matters for MagSafe wallets, car mounts, etc. The Classic Hybrid has 1,500g of magnetic hold, and the Atelier has 1,400g.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Classic Hybrid Magnetic Case for iPhone Duo is 15% off.

The same two incredible cases come in iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max versions, and they also fit the iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max. The ESR Classic Hybrid Magnetic Case with Camera Control and Flex Stand has a clear back, a TPU frame, and a PU anti-yellowing coating. In simple terms, TPU is the flexible, shock-absorbing plastic used in most case frames, and it’s also what usually turns clear cases slightly yellow the longer you use them, so ESR adds a polyurethane (PU) coating to shield it. ESR upgraded the case’s UV protection for longer-lasting resistance to yellowing, and it’s SGS-certified for anti-yellowing. A clear case is supposed to show off your iPhone’s color, so staying clear longer is the whole point. The ESR Atelier Vegan Leather Magnetic Case with Flex Stand retains the same soft silicone leather and stain-resistant finish as the iPhone Duo version.

On these models, the Flex Stand adjusts from 15 to 69 degrees for portrait and landscape viewing. That has you covered for StandBy mode on your nightstand and a show over your lunch break, with no separate stand to carry around.

Protection is where the two cases differ. ESR rates the Classic Hybrid for 4x military-grade protection with 16-foot drop protection, plus a full-coverage camera bar. The Atelier is rated for 3x military-grade protection, including 12-foot drop protection, and features a soft microfiber lining. Military-grade refers to the MIL-STD-810 drop test, which uses a 4-foot drop, so 4x and 3x mean ESR rates the cases for four and three times that height. Both include a built-in Camera Control cover and raised edges, and both use a precise magnetic ring layout that automatically aligns with MagSafe chargers, car mounts, wallets, and batteries.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Classic Hybrid Magnetic Case is up to 28% off, and the ESR Atelier Vegan Leather Magnetic Case is up to 37% off.

A case protects everything except the part you touch all day. The ESR UltraFit Armorite Pro Screen Protector covers the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, and the name is worth unpacking. Armorite is ESR’s line of toughened screen protectors, and the Pro version is made with Accessory Glass by Corning™. Corning has made the durable glass in Apple products since the very first iPhone, so in non-tech speak, this is glass from a trustworthy name rather than generic tempered glass.

Why it matters: ESR says the protector delivers 10x the impact absorption of generic protectors, and Corning’s lab testing shows up to 2x better scratch performance and up to 25% less scratch visibility for its Accessory Glass. When you drop your iPhone or toss it in a pocket with your keys, the protector takes the hit instead of your screen. An anti-reflective coating reduces light reflection to just 2.3% while maintaining 94% optical transmittance, resulting in less glare outside and truer color. Edge-to-edge coverage leaves no gaps for dust to collect.

Installation is the part most people dread on a brand-new iPhone, and ESR’s UltraFit tray handles it in two steps. Pull the tab, and the tray’s design clears dust and pushes out air bubbles as the glass goes down. Long gone are the days when you needed “professional installation” for a screen protector to look great.

Black Friday deal: The ESR UltraFit Armorite Pro Screen Protector is 15% off.

Holiday travel usually means one open outlet, an iPhone, a laptop, an e-reader, etc., that all need power, and cables left at home. The ESR Xtend 45W Retractable Charger builds the cable in. It has a braided cable that extends to 3.1 feet and fully retracts into the charger, and ESR rates it for 20,000 pulls and 10,000 bends. An extra USB-C port lets a second device charge simultaneously. 9to5Mac’s Michael Burkhardt went hands-on with the Xtend 45W earlier this month and said it’s an excellent iPhone fast charger on the go.

It’s rated at 45 watts and delivers up to 60 watts of dynamic power, enough to fast-charge phones and laptops, and it works with iPhone Duo, iPhone 15 through 18, and Android phones like Galaxy and Pixel. It supports PD 3.2 AVS, which in plain English means the charger and your device talk to each other, and the charger fine-tunes the power it sends to exactly what that device asks for. ESR says it can charge an iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max to 50% in about 15 minutes. It’s also TÜV-certified, meaning an independent testing organization has verified its safety features.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Xtend 45W Retractable Charger is up to 32% off from November 20 through December 1.

For the student or anyone who does real work on an iPad, the ESR Shift Keyboard Case makes for an incredible gift. The Bluetooth keyboard attaches magnetically and comes off when you don’t need it, so you can type an essay at a desk, then pull the keyboard away to watch something on the couch or sketch with the iPad flat on a table.

ESR built the Shift around five modes designed to make your iPad even more versatile. Productivity mode lets you detach the keyboard and type over Bluetooth, so the iPad can sit on a desk while the keyboard sits on your lap. Landscape mode adjusts from 20 to 75 degrees for typing and watching, Portrait mode holds 70 degrees for reading, browsing in Safari, or making a FaceTime call, and Drawing mode drops to a stable 20 degrees for sketching and editing with your Apple Pencil. Hands-On mode lets you hold the iPad like a regular tablet. An iPad is a laptop one minute and a tablet the next, and the Shift is designed to keep up with all of your iPad use cases.

For a student, that means taking notes in class with the keyboard attached, then detaching it to annotate a PDF or review flashcards on the couch. For someone who travels for work, it means answering email on a tray table, then pulling the keyboard off to watch a movie on the flight home. One case covers both, and the keyboard pairs and reconnects easily when you snap it back on.

The trackpad is fully clickable and supports all the multi-touch gestures you already use on your iPad. Apple Pencil gets a home too. ESR’s Dual Smart Pencil Storage uses a magnetic holder and an elastic sleeve, so your Pencil stays with your iPad instead of rolling around the bottom of your bag. Its Air Guard corners protect your iPad when it’s stowed away.

The ESR Shift Keyboard Case comes in versions for iPad Pro 11-inch and 13-inch (M4 and M5), iPad Air 11-inch and 13-inch (including the new M4 models), and iPad (A16), so whichever iPad you’re trying to take to the next level of productivity, there’s a Shift that fits it.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Shift Keyboard Case is up to 25% off, depending on your iPad model.

Have you ever dropped your AirPods case and watched the earbuds go flying? With the Cyber FlickLock, you won’t have to worry about that. We’ve covered FlickLock in MagSafe Monday before, but let’s recap it.

When the internal latch is engaged, the magnets line up to attract each other and hold the lid shut with maximum force, adding a second layer of security. Slide the button, and the magnets shift to repel each other, so the lid pops open with one hand. ESR says the slide mechanism has been tested over 20,000 times.

The result is that your AirPods stay in the case if you drop it. Again, it’s extremely strong, but extremely easy to unlock with one hand.

The ESR Cyber FlickLock Magnetic Case is extremely durable and has a clip hook, so you can hang your AirPods on a backpack while hiking or cycling. The ESR Pulse FlickLock Magnetic Case brings the same lock in a range of vibrant colors with a carrying lanyard, so you can wear your AirPods on your wrist or attach them to a bag. Both cases come in versions for AirPods Pro 3, AirPods Pro 2 and 1, and AirPods 5 and 4. No matter which AirPods you or your loved one have, this is the case everyone will love.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Cyber FlickLock and Pulse FlickLock Magnetic Cases are both 20% off.

The ESR Equinox Watch Band is a quick pick for anyone who works out in the morning while tracking progress with Apple Watch, then heads to the office. A pin-and-fold lock keeps it secure, and it’s made from HNBR, a durable, skin-friendly synthetic rubber that resists water and tearing, with ventilation cutouts for all-day comfort. It fits 44mm, 45mm, 46mm, and 49mm models across Apple Watch Ultra 1 through 4, Series 4 through 12, and SE 1 through 3, and it comes in several colors to match your outfit or your mood that day.

The best gifts are the ones that get used every day, and accessories are the part of the Apple experience people live with the most. A case that props up a foldable, a screen protector made with Corning glass, a charger with a built-in cable, and an AirPods case that stays closed even when dropped check all the boxes. ESR truly makes something for everyone and is one of the most trusted names in the Apple accessories ecosystem.

#3253. Salesforce vs. ServiceNow: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?

Salesforce trades at a lower forward P/E than ServiceNow, yet ServiceNow is growing revenue faster, forcing investors to weigh price against momentum.

By Sara Appino – Updated Nov 20, 2026 at 4:27PM EST

10 stocks we like better than Salesforce ›

The shift toward enterprise automation and artificial intelligence has created a fierce battle between two cloud software titans. Investors choosing between Salesforce (CRM -1.47%) and ServiceNow (NOW -1.42%) must decide which platform offers better value.

Salesforce dominates the customer relationship management space, helping businesses track every client interaction. ServiceNow specializes in streamlining back-office workflows, from IT support to HR tasks. Both companies are now racing to integrate generative AI into their ecosystems, making this a pivotal comparison for investors seeking growth in tech stocks.

Salesforce provides cloud-based software that connects sales, marketing, and IT on a single platform to serve over 150,000 companies. It has recently prioritized AI integration through a major partnership with Microsoft (MSFT -2.77%) for "Copilotforce," which combines customer context with AI experiences. The company continues expanding its reach through acquisitions such as Braze (BRZE +0.09%) to deepen engagement. Salesforce serves businesses of all sizes globally, and no single customer accounts for more than 10% of its total revenue.

In the 12 months ended July 31, 2026, revenue reached approximately $43.9 billion, representing growth of nearly 11.2% over the prior period. The company also generated net income of roughly $9.7 billion, which reflects a net margin of close to 22%. This growth trend has been supported by a steady increase in revenue from $34.9 billion just two years ago. The business focuses on maintaining profitability while scaling its cloud ecosystem and proprietary AI tools.

As of its January 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 0.3x, which compares total debt to shareholder equity. The current ratio, a measure of how well a company covers short-term debts with short-term assets, is approximately 0.8x. In the fiscal year ended Jan. 31, 2026, free cash flow was nearly $14.4 billion. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 23.4% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

ServiceNow offers an AI platform designed to automate enterprise work across departments including IT, human resources, and finance. The company focuses on large enterprise clients, ending recent periods with over 600 customers spending more than $5 million annually. It maintains strategic partnerships with Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) and Accenture (ACN +1.19%) to drive AI-driven workflow integrations for its 8,700 total customers. This strategy targets a growing presence in the public sector and large organizations seeking efficient digital transformation.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached close to $15.4 billion, marking revenue growth of approximately 21.8% over the preceding year. ServiceNow reported net income of nearly $1.4 billion for this period, yielding a net margin of approximately 9.4%. While its net margin is lower than its rival, the company has consistently increased its top line from $9.0 billion two years prior. This expansion reflects robust demand for workflow automation tools across global markets.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0.2x. The current ratio, which measures the ability to cover short-term obligations using liquid assets, is roughly 1.0x, and free cash flow reached nearly $4.6 billion in the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 35.9% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

Salesforce faces intense competition from established software vendors and AI-native firms entering the customer relationship management space. Integrating large-scale acquisitions like Braze involves execution risks that could disrupt operations if not managed carefully. The company also navigates cybersecurity threats and potential volatility from shifting its pricing models toward consumption-based structures.

ServiceNow must prove it can continue competing effectively as the AI market evolves rapidly. The company relies on third-party cloud providers and faces regulatory scrutiny related to its growing government contracting business. Additionally, any failure to realize benefits from its aggressive merger and acquisition strategy could impact future growth prospects if integration costs exceed the value gained.

Salesforce appears more attractively priced on a relative basis, carrying a lower Forward P/E based on future earnings estimates and a lower P/S ratio measuring value against sales over the past twelve months.

Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

I'd go with ServiceNow. Management expects its AI products to reach $1.7 billion in yearly contracts by the end of this year, and they run on software that big companies rely on for everyday work like IT and HR requests. That software is a very sticky product, with an impressive 98% renewal rate, meaning almost all customers sign up again.

ServiceNow's AI business is growing fast, and overall sales are still rising rapidly. The stock plunged after its latest earnings report, as investors worried about slower growth in future contracts and about AI hurting software companies. But management has raised its AI goal twice this year, and the drop leaves the shares well below where they traded before.

To be fair to Salesforce, it is the cheaper stock and it is buying back a lot of its own shares. Its AI products are also catching on. But its sales are growing more slowly, and part of that growth came from buying another company. For long-term investors, ServiceNow offers a fast-growing AI business on top of software customers rarely leave, at a lower price after the recent sell-off.

#3252. Top Wall Street analysts believe in the growth potential of these 3 stocks

Geopolitical uncertainty in the Middle East and soaring bond yields weighed on global markets this past week. And investors are closely assessing the valuations of artificial intelligence stocks amid concerns about the sustainability of high spending on AI infrastructure.

Despite those continued challenges, top Wall Street analysts are bullish on the prospects of several stocks due to their long-run growth potential and exposure to lucrative business lines, including AI.

Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

Cybersecurity company CrowdStrike Holdings (CRWD) is this week's first stock pick. The company is scheduled to announce fiscal second-quarter results on August 26.

Ahead of Q2 FY27 earnings, Truist analyst Junaid Siddiqui reiterated a buy rating on CrowdStrike stock and raised his price target to $245 from $187.50. Following CrowdStrike's impressive fiscal first-quarter performance and guidance raise, Siddiqui expects another strong quarter.

The 5-star analyst's optimism is backed by continued strength in Falcon Flex adoption and encouraging large deal activity. Siddiqui also cited continued momentum across emerging products. With the FY27 outlook assuming persistent strength in CrowdStrike's net new annual recurring revenue (ARR), Siddiqui is more focused on the longevity of key growth catalysts such as Falcon Flex adoption, platform consolidation and AI-led demand.

The analyst highlighted that talks with partners were encouraging, with pipeline generation and momentum in large deals remaining healthy in the fiscal second quarter despite tough, year-over-year comparisons.

"We continue to view CrowdStrike as one of the primary beneficiaries of platform consolidation, though we expect investors to remain focused on competitive dynamics and whether current growth levels represent a new baseline or a period of demand acceleration," the analyst said.

Siddiqui ranks No. 226 among more than 12,400 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 80% of the time, delivering an average return of about 40%. See CrowdStrike Financials on TipRanks.

Shares of personal computer maker Dell Technologies (DELL) have rallied 251% this year, driven by strong demand for AI servers. Recently, Evercore analyst Amit Daryanani reiterated a buy rating on DELL and raised his price target to $550 from $500.

The 5-star analyst contends that while Dell's AI compute segment is getting investors' attention, the company's Storage business is underappreciated and well-positioned to drive revenue and profit acceleration. Daryanani expects the storage business to see higher demand once enterprises start to bring workload back on-premises.

The analyst highlighted that Dell's Storage business, estimated to account for only 10% of FY27 revenue, is one of the factors that could help improve profit margins, given its higher profitability compared to AI servers. Daryanani estimates that the Storage business's operating margin is currently in the low-20% range, while margins for the AI server and traditional server businesses are in the mid-single-digit and mid-teens range, respectively.

Overall, Daryanani views the Storage business as an important catalyst for three reasons: Dell has one of the broadest storage portfolios in the industry; Storage has a significantly higher margin profile than AI servers; and the shift toward proprietary, software-defined storage and AI-focused platforms.

"We think DELL's storage business is becoming increasingly strategic as AI infrastructure deployments move beyond GPU procurement and toward full stack + AI-ready architectures," said Daryanani.

Daryanani ranks No. 19 among more than 12,400 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 71% of the time, delivering an average return of 38.70%. See Dell Technologies Statistics on TipRanks.

SanDisk (SNDK) is benefiting from AI-driven demand for its memory and storage products. Following the company's 2026 Investor Day event, J.P. Morgan analyst Harlan Sur resumed research coverage of SNDK with a buy rating (it was earlier, "Not Rated") and a price target of $2,250.

The 5-star analyst believes SanDisk is well-positioned to capitalize on a structural inflection reached in NAND demand, driven by strong growth in AI inference. Sur's bullishness is based on three key factors.

First, Sur believes that SanDisk's New Business Model (NBM) framework (or long-term agreements) has enhanced its margin profile and reduced cyclicality. SNDK's eight signed NBMs represent a total contract value of $94 billion and a gross margin of about 80%, even at the floor pricing.

Second, Sur highlighted the growing NAND market and expects the total addressable market to surge from about $70 billion in calendar year 2025 to over $300 billion in 2026 and about $500 billion in 2027. Importantly, the analyst noted that data centers are the largest driver of NAND growth, as hyperscalers increasingly deploy flash for AI inference workloads.

Finally, Sur is optimistic on SanDisk due to its technology dominance. The company's BiCS10 technology is sampling ahead of schedule and has 65% more bits per wafer than BiCS8, the analyst said. Also, Sur expects SanDisk's High Bandwidth Flash to become a differentiated memory platform for AI inference.

"Layered on top, mgmt's commitment to returning 100% of excess cash flow to shareholders should drive an aggressive share count reduction trajectory that further amplifies EPS growth on a per-share basis," said Sur.

Sur ranks No. 15 among more than 12,400 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 71% of the time, delivering an average return of 43.20%. See SanDisk Ownership Structure on TipRanks.
